items.t: Every first-page card is labelled with the board sub-area "Yaletown" and a Vancouver mailing address, on streets including Beach Crescent, Marinaside Crescent, Mainland Street, Cambie Street, Howe Street, Homer Street, Richards Street and Beach Avenue — a strata-condo page for Yaletown, the downtown Vancouver neighbourhood on the north shore of False Creek, not a detached-house page and not a whole-downtown page.

Municipal frame: Yaletown is inside the City of Vancouver, within the City's "Downtown" local area, and the City separately regulates its historic core as the Yaletown Historic Area (HA-3). On the City's heritage-area description, Yaletown is bordered by Homer and Nelson streets to the north and east, and Cambie, Mainland and Drake streets to the south and west.

Where the condo stock concentrates: two shelves. The False Creek waterfront shelf — Beach Crescent, Homer Mews and Marinaside Crescent towers (King's Landing, Crestmark I and II, Azura 2) facing David Lam Park, George Wainborn Park and the seawall — and the inland tower shelf on Mainland, Homer, Cambie and Richards Streets (Yaletown Park 3, The Bentley, City Crest, Waterworks, Pacific Landmark II), plus the heritage warehouse-conversion lofts of the Homer Street core (The Murchies).

Character, per the City: Yaletown gets its special character from its compact collection of buildings made of heavy timber, brick and concrete, with narrow streets and covered loading docks that serve as public space; the HA-3 Historic Area District Schedule encourages the conversion and renovation of its buildings and compatible new buildings, to produce a mix of commercial, industrial and residential uses.

Transit: Yaletown–Roundhouse Station on the Canada Line serves the neighbourhood — TransLink's SkyTrain station listing places it in the Canada Line sequence between Vancouver City Centre and Olympic Village Stations, on both the Waterfront–YVR/Airport and Waterfront–Richmond–Brighouse branches.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Yaletown

items.t: City plans, zoning and heritage: Yaletown sits inside the City of Vancouver's Zoning and Development By-law framework, and its historic core is the Yaletown Historic Area (HA-3): the City has created regulations and companion design guidelines to preserve the historic fabric of its protected areas (Chinatown, Gastown, Shaughnessy and Yaletown), and the HA-3 schedule encourages conversion and renovation of Yaletown's heavy-timber, brick and concrete buildings and compatible new buildings for a mix of commercial, industrial and residential uses. A renovation plan for a warehouse-conversion loft (The Murchies shelf) is governed by that heritage frame, not just the strata bylaws.
Price a prepaid-lease building against its lease term, not against freehold comparables, and read the title and strata plan for the exact unit before anything else.

Vancouver property taxes: advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes were due July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid balances after the main-tax deadline — the City collects twice a year, the second business day of February and of July.

Empty Homes Tax (Vancouver): every Vancouver residential owner must submit an annual property status declaration on or before the 2nd business day in February under Vacancy Tax By-law No. 11674; a property with no declaration is deemed vacant, and a vacancy tax unpaid as of the 10th business day of April bears a 5% penalty. The rate cited by secondary sources for the current reference year is 3% of assessed value; the City pages reviewed did not state the rate, so it is secondary-sourced and not City-verified. An investor-buyer needs the declaration calendar explained before closing, not after.

blocks.text: Good to know about Yaletown

items.t: The two sources for Yaletown's biggest inland complex do not agree with each other. Yaletown Park 3 at 977 Mainland Street is 266 units / BCS2143 in the building directory and 272 units / BCS2103 on a strata-manager's building-data page — same developer (Wall Financial), same 2007 completion, different count and plan number. Anyone quoting either figure as settled has read only one source.

City Crest's unit count has the same disease, smaller. One building source gives 143 units for 1155 Homer Street; an entire-floor sales document for the same building gives 135 total units over 29 floors. The 1994 build year and Freehold Strata title agree in both.

Waterworks is one building inside a much bigger strata. The 1008 Cambie Street tower holds 209 units, but its strata complex totals 535 units across Cambie Street and Expo Boulevard addresses — a Waterworks buyer's levies and votes are set at complex scale, not tower scale.

Crestmark II cannot decide what year it was built. A building source gives 1997 (22 storeys, 221 units) for 1228 Marinaside Crescent, one current listing agrees at 1997, and another current listing for the same address gives 1998.

Yaletown's character is a planning rule, not a vibe. The City's own description — heavy timber, brick and concrete buildings, narrow streets, covered loading docks serving as public space — is written into the HA-3 heritage frame that governs conversions and new buildings, which is why the Homer Street loft shelf (The Murchies, 1912, converted 1997) looks and trades differently from the Marinaside towers.

What trades here

items.t: Airspace subdivision as the operative form: on the downtown peninsula, the division that matters after a project is built is airspace subdivision — separate airspace parcels for residential, commercial and parking components within one development — not ground-lot subdivision under the house-lot model. A Yaletown condo buyer owns a strata lot inside that airspace/strata structure; there is no ground lot to diligence separately from the strata documents.

Built form on the parcels: the historic core's stock is heavy-timber, brick and concrete warehouse-era buildings, converted and renovated under the HA-3 schedule, mixed with compatible newer buildings.
The False Creek South City ground-lease position is south-shore ground and does not apply to Yaletown.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Yaletown

items.t: Heritage district — Yaletown Historic Area (HA-3): the Historic Area District Schedule for Yaletown (HA-3) encourages the conversion and renovation of its buildings and compatible new buildings, to produce a mix of commercial, industrial and residential uses, under the City's heritage-area regulations and companion design guidelines. Exterior change and redevelopment on Yaletown parcels starts with HA-3, not the base district alone.

Downtown districts (DD / CD-1 frame): Yaletown development parcels sit in the City of Vancouver's downtown district frame (DD / CD-1, per the downtown-ve lots precedent); a CD-1 is a site-specific comprehensive district, so the parcel's own CD-1 bylaw — not a generic density figure — governs what its land can hold. Parcel-level district and CD-1 text: confirm on the parcel's bylaw before pricing any redevelopment.

Subdivision — Subdivision By-law No. 5208, fees by No. 14538 (verified Vancouver frame): Vancouver subdivision runs under Subdivision By-law No. 5208 with fees under By-law No. 14538; on downtown ground the operative division is airspace subdivision, confirmed parcel by parcel with the City.
SSMUH / house-lot subdivision potential: No SSMUH figure is asserted for Yaletown ground.

Strata block (the operative diligence for Yaletown condo land): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw. Read the depreciation report, contingency fund and any lease or rental-restriction bylaws off the strata documents.
Property taxes (City of Vancouver): advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes were due July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid balances after the main-tax deadline.

blocks.text: Good to know about Yaletown

items.t: The loading docks are the public space: Yaletown's character, per the City, comes from heavy-timber, brick and concrete buildings with narrow streets whose covered loading docks serve as public space — the heritage frame (HA-3) protects that fabric, which is why exterior change here is a permit question, not just a strata question.

One school sits on a boundary street: Elsie Roy Elementary is at 150 Drake St, and Drake is one of the streets the City uses to define Yaletown's edge — a Yaletown address and a Yaletown catchment are still two different checks, and only the school's existence and address are confirmed here.

faq.a: Four counted buildings state Freehold Strata in their sources — Azura 2 (1495 Richards Street), The Bentley (1001 Homer Street), City Crest (1155 Homer Street) and Pacific Landmark II (930 Cambie Street).
faq.q: Are Yaletown condos freehold or leasehold?

faq.a: Both agree on Wall Financial Corporation as developer and 2007 completion.
faq.q: How many units are in Yaletown Park 3, really?

faq.a: Long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, and the directory positions for Yaletown Park 3, City Crest and Pacific Landmark II all record rentals allowed. Pets differ by building and pet bylaws remain enforceable: the directory records pets allowed at King's Landing and Yaletown Park 3 (2 pets; 1 dog and 1 cat), a listing records pets welcome at The Bentley and "Cats OK" at Crestmark II, while Pacific Landmark II's directory line is pets not allowed — read the registered bylaws on the Form B for the building you are buying.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Yaletown condo, and can I bring a dog?

faq.a: Four townhouse-form units inside Yaletown Park 3, a 29-level Wall Financial tower strata.
faq.q: I saw townhouses listed at 977 Mainland Street — what are they?

faq.a: It varies by building. Four of the 10 counted buildings state Freehold Strata in their sources.
faq.q: Is a Yaletown condo freehold or leasehold?

faq.a: A long-term rental-restriction bylaw is void since November 24, 2022 in any BC strata; short-term rentals can still be restricted.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Yaletown unit long-term?

faq.a: Yes — the HA-3 schedule and the City's heritage-area regulations govern changes to the warehouse-era stock (heavy timber, brick, concrete).
faq.q: Does the heritage area limit what I can do with a Yaletown loft?

faq.a: On the City of Vancouver's own heritage-area description, Yaletown is bordered by Homer and Nelson streets to the north and east, and Cambie, Mainland, and Drake streets to the south and west, on the north shore of False Creek in downtown Vancouver.
